set.body:
Raised by independent review while Epic 1 is in progress. Measured against the working tree.

The volume_stencil provider is a genuine fix - linear and fast:

  p=  8000  0.50s   61.9 us/voxel
  p= 27000  0.69s   25.6
  p= 64000  1.45s   22.6
  p= 97336  2.35s   24.1   (radius 6.1mm, spacing 3mm)

The coordinate_cells provider is not. It is superlinear and 10-25x slower per voxel:

  p=  8000  1.29s  161.9 us/voxel
  p= 27000  6.29s  233.1
  p= 50653 14.55s  287.3   (radius 2.1, unit grid)

For reference the all-pairs loop it replaced was 1.89s at p=8000 and 7.03s at p=15625, so at p=8000 the new provider is only ~1.5x faster than the quadratic code it replaced.

Cause - confirmed by a discriminating experiment

.coordinate_ball_members (R/support-index.R:195-228) builds `groups <- split(seq_len(n), keys)` with CHARACTER keys, then per centre evaluates `groups[candidate_keys]`. Character indexing of a list calls match() against all of names(groups), so the per-centre cost is O(n_groups) and the total is O(p x n_groups) - quadratic in p at fixed cell occupancy.

Holding p = 19683 fixed and varying only the radius (hence n_groups):

  radius  n_groups  mean|support|   total   lookup-only
    1.1     15625        6.8       11.62s     8.49s   <- 73% of runtime
    2.1      2197       30.6        4.71s        -
    4.1       343      217.6        4.78s     2.31s   <- 48% of runtime
    8.1        64     1539.2       16.84s        -
   16.1         8     7980.0       33.91s     2.86s

Lookup-only cost tracks n_groups, not support size. The small-radius case is pathological: 11.6s to find supports averaging under 7 voxels.

Why it still matters even though volume is fast

- The README headline example uses abstract_domain() + searchlights(), which routes to coordinate_cells.
- The 50k acceptance test (tests/testthat/test-support-index.R:125-134) uses volume_domain, i.e. the fast provider, and asserts only pair_pattern_nnz < p^2/1000 - a STORAGE bound. Epic 1 acceptance says "without quadratic-in-p allocation", so time is not gated anywhere.
- coordinate_cells is covered only by the tiny fixture at line 24.

Fix

Replace character cell keys with integer cell codes and resolve all centres in one vectorised match() (or order()/rle bucketing) so lookup is O(p k) rather than O(p x n_groups). Then scale-test the coordinate provider, not only the volume one.

Minor, same file: R/frame.R:115 uses `exists("support_index", inherits = FALSE)` to detect which branch ran. It is correct today but fragile - prefer initialising support_index <- NULL and testing is.null(). Also note voxels()/regions()/whole_brain() frames now carry no support_index, so the "one canonical support topology" is currently searchlight-only.
set.title: coordinate_cells support provider retains an O(p x n_groups) term via character-keyed list lookup
